title: [SEP2-5] Any single DM member can rewrite the admission host's member list, silently cutting others
description: Review finding SEP2-5: Any single DM member can rewrite the admission host's member list, silently cutting others off at relays or handing the admission key to non-members (lens SEP2). Location: spec/04-access-control.md:158, :259; spec/02-identity.md:452. Fix: Only the removal half holds. Adding non-members grants nothing beyond what any member can already do: every member holds the `ChannelAdmissionKey` seed (12:57 "Anyone who holds a `ChannelAdmissionKey` ... can compute the token"), so a hostile member can give it to anyone directly, and an added outsider still cannot read without MLS. That half is REJECTED. The removal half is real. A DM has no "remove another member" operation (04:257-259 define only self-Remove; 02:452 allows Removes only of revoked devices), yet 04:158 lets any one listed member drop any DID, and the host then rotates and refuses that DID the key. The fix follows from existing rules: the host accepts a `DMMembers` replacement that drops a DID only if (i) the signer is that DID (self-leave), or (ii) the dropped DID's resolved DID document has no current device keys (revoked/offboarded, matching 02:452). Additions remain accepted from any listed member. Change 04:259 so the leaving member's client sends its own `DMMembers` replacement, not the committer's. Full text: notes/review2/SEP2-verified.md and notes/review2/SEP2.md.
